headline: High: Rasa’s allowlisted egress and multi-channel inputs create default leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with the docs-only ai-engineering-hub.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and tagged for agents/MCP/RAG, so it may emit or route content that Rasa could ingest through chat channels. Rasa exposes multiple external message surfaces, making instruction-like content from A plausible to reach B. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into a Rasa channel or RAG source
IF Rasa treats inbound message text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Disable any auto-ingest from A into B
Require human review before forwarding A outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all bridged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared data classes and has no egress, but B handles text and voice and can send data through allowlisted APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or message bridge, A-generated content can enter B and then leave via external channels. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF A outputs are forwarded into B’s conversation context
IF B relays that context to any listed API channel
mitigations: Remove any shared workspace or clipboard bridge
Redact secrets before forwarding content to B
Turn off outbound integrations not needed for the test

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write surfaces and B explicitly does not support multiple instances, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. The main overlap is conceptual rather than operational: A is an agent/RAG repo and B is a chatbot framework with allowlisted channels. Without shared mutable resources, the pairwise conflict pathway is weak.
conditions: IF both are deployed against the same mutable backend or workspace
IF an orchestrator adds shared write access not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid shared databases or git repos
Document ownership of each mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a customer-support bot framework that can act on inbound dialogue, while A is an agent/RAG-oriented repo that may generate content for downstream use. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF A-generated text is used as B’s source of truth
IF B responds or routes actions without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a validation step before B uses A output
Require citations or source links for A-derived claims
Limit B to draft-only responses until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. A is open-source with no data classes touched; B handles text/voice and exposes messaging APIs, but the profiles do not show regulated data or conflicting compliance regimes. Because the evidence is sparse, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through B
IF deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Review retention settings on each integration
Document data-class handling for each channel
